errors.text: The proposed W-Mo-Ta-Nb-V alloy is not a Group IV-V alloy family: W and Mo are Group VI elements, and the composition omits the target Group IV elements Hf, Ti, and Zr.

The hypothesis replaces hydride-based ink extrusion, hydrogen de-binding, vacuum sintering, oxygen gettering, and quenching with LPBF and precipitation aging, so it does not reconstruct the target manufacturing route.
It misses the central target microstructure: an oxygen-strengthened, metastable single beta-BCC phase retained by water quenching rather than a BCC matrix containing coherent B2 nanoprecipitates.
The evidence supports LPBF of WMoTaNbV, SCCP strengthening, and inverted BCC+B2 structures in separate contexts, but does not establish that their combination will occur in LPBF W20Mo20Ta20Nb20V20.

Mitigation of interstitial-impurity brittleness by coherent B2 precipitates is asserted without direct supporting evidence; the cited SCCP mechanism concerns strength-ductility optimization and crack initiation, not controlled oxygen strengthening or interstitial tolerance.
